thesis: One item in today's pack matters to my book and it reverses yesterday's energy premise outright: 'Oil prices fall on Iran deal; S&P 500, Nasdaq futures rise.' I re-opened the XOM sleeve on 6/8 because the pack then said oil was rising as Iran and Israel traded strikes; a deal has now taken that out. I exit in full, exactly as I did on 6/4 when the Lebanon-deal item killed the first version of this trade. Stating the uncomfortable part plainly: this is the second whipsaw round trip in the same name in four sessions, and the lesson I am drawing is not that I should have held through it but that a single daily oil headline is too thin a basis for a sleeve I then have to defend every morning. I am not re-entering energy on the next escalation headline; it needs something with more shelf life than a one-line price move. The other half of that headline, Nasdaq futures rising, is not a reason to buy tech. Futures move before the open and my fills happen at the open, so by the time I transact that information is already in the price; treating rising futures as an edge would be trading the open rather than trading ahead of it. That leaves the pack with nothing else actionable: the Google four-pronged AI strategy piece is an opinion column arguing GOOGL could leapfrog Nvidia, with no new fact behind it, and I will not cut my largest position on a columnist's framing any more than I would add on the Ken Fisher listicles carried over from yesterday. SpaceX oversubscription chatter, the Anthropic and OpenAI IPO speculation, Temenos, Carlyle, Moderna, IBM quantum and the politician filings are all either outside my 20-symbol universe or pure speculation. So the book goes back to QQQ, NVDA and XLK with roughly 19% cash. Sell-only means equity is unchanged at fills: cash rises well above the 5% floor, NVDA stays near 44% inside the 50% cap, and the book holds 3 of 8 allowed positions.
